topic: 检查当前项目的开发进度、代码完成度、前端 UI 与后端接口及工作流程控制的吻合度，并判断是否体验完整、是否可交付客户

relevant_files.summary: Defines the semantic delivery hard gate, including workflow confirmation, chat routes, metrics route, local check scripts, packaging dry-run, and authority-alignment anchors.
Checks workflow/runtime/docs contract alignment across README, runbooks, CI workflows, and launcher semantics.
Builds the deterministic GO/NO_GO release artifact and points to the authoritative local desktop and src-ts gates.
Defines the authoritative backend/local release gate: lint, format, typecheck, phase4 coverage, release integration tests.
Defines the authoritative desktop/local release gate, sidecar validation, and packaging dry-run entrypoints.
Desktop workflow API resolves standard vs ui-bridge paths without ad hoc branching.
Desktop client uses /workflow/rollback and /checkpoint/* paths that now match backend route registry.
Desktop admin service APIs target /admin/mcp/services* paths aligned with backend.
Desktop config client uses GET/PUT /config, GET/PUT /config/secrets, and POST /config/reload to match platform routes.
Registers workflow, rollback, checkpoint, and ui-bridge workflow endpoints.
Registers config and metrics routes expected by release gate and desktop frontend.
Covers destructive confirm_required gating, lifecycle pause, checkpoint list, and quick rollback flow.
Asserts desktop client is hitting current workflow rollback/checkpoint endpoints and workspace-aware payloads.
Covers writer-facing workflow UX continuity such as workspace anchoring, workflow IDs, and sidebar entrypoints.
Makes the runtime split explicit: local authority is Node, packaged compatibility runtime is Python.
Documents the supported local runtime, packaged compatibility fallback, and unsigned dry-run packaging boundary.
Still shows unchecked umbrella phases even though newer closure sessions exist; this reads as stale bookkeeping, not a current product blocker.

findings.title: Current checkout still behaves like a late-stage, technically deliverable repository
findings.detail: The project does not look like it is in heavy active churn. The present worktree is effectively clean, the authoritative semantic gate and authority-alignment check both pass today, and both official local release entrypoints reproduce green results on the current checkout.

findings.title: Frontend workflow/config/admin paths are materially aligned with backend route registration and exercised by tests
findings.detail: Desktop APIs call /workflow, /ui-bridge/workflow, /workflow/rollback, /checkpoint/*, /admin/mcp/services*, and /config* paths that are registered on the backend and covered by route/integration tests. This materially reduces the risk of UI/back-end contract drift in the customer path.

findings.title: Workflow control-plane behavior has concrete hard-gate and rollback evidence rather than placeholder wiring
findings.detail: The backend workflow endpoint tests explicitly verify destructive confirm_required gating, lifecycle pause/checkpoint creation, checkpoint listing, and rollback. Desktop tests also verify the same control-plane endpoints. This is a strong objective signal that workflow orchestration is not merely scaffolded.

findings.title: The main remaining technical caveat is packaging/runtime compatibility, not primary product completeness
findings.detail: The current contract is Node-first for local authoritative runtime, but packaged desktop execution still expects a Python compatibility sidecar artifact for the current target. This is documented and validated, yet it remains a release-process caveat and a future simplification target rather than a blocker for current unsigned delivery proof.

findings.title: A few non-primary modules still expose mock/fallback or explicit non-implemented branches
findings.detail: Examples include LLMService.embed throwing a documented not-supported error in favor of EmbeddingService, local embedding falling back when an optional backend is absent, and some narrative evaluators returning mock values when no LLM client is configured. These read as bounded degradation paths, but they weaken any claim that every advanced analysis feature is equally production-hardened.

findings.title: One old migration umbrella session still looks active even though newer closure work has already landed
findings.detail: The stale active migration TODO list is more of an audit/bookkeeping smell than a product readiness blocker, because newer targeted delivery-readiness and hotspot sessions are fully checked and today’s executable gates are green. Still, it can confuse a client-side audit if presented raw.

risks.risk: Packaged desktop currently relies on a Python compatibility sidecar artifact for the target triple.
risks.impact: Does not block current technical delivery evidence, but keeps packaging/sign-off process more fragile than a pure Node-first bundle.

risks.risk: Some advanced narrative/embedding branches still degrade to mock or explicit fallback behavior when optional runtime dependencies are absent.
risks.impact: Could reduce the completeness of non-core analytical features in under-configured environments.

risks.risk: Old migration master workflow remains marked active with unchecked umbrella tasks.
risks.impact: Primarily an audit/readability issue; may imply unfinished transition if reviewed without newer context.

verdict_tendency.judgment: From a technical implementation and verification perspective, the current repository looks materially finished enough for customer delivery. The strongest signals are current-date green gates, aligned desktop/backend workflow-control contracts, passing local release checks, and a nearly clean worktree. Remaining issues are caveats around packaged compatibility/runtime process and a few bounded fallback branches, not evidence of an unstable main product path.
limits: This exploration did not perform a manual interactive desktop click-through or signed external packaging flow.
Release summary artifacts in repo are still dated 2026-04-12; today’s confidence comes from rerunning the authoritative local gates rather than regenerating those artifacts.

questions_for_analysis: Business/product perspective should decide whether the packaged Python compatibility sidecar is acceptable in the customer delivery narrative.
UX/product perspective should verify subjective completeness of the writer journey via a manual interactive run, because technical tests cannot fully substitute for hands-on experience evaluation.
